items.followUp: Write the formulae of hydrochloric acid and glucose.

rubric.why: The formula of sulphuric acid is required.
The formula of sugar (sucrose) is required.

items.followUp: Define a cation and explain how it is formed.

rubric.why: An anion is identified by its negative charge.
rubric.description: Defines an anion as a negatively charged ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a negative ion.

rubric.why: An anion forms when an atom or group gains electrons.
rubric.description: Explains formation by gain of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electrons are gained.

modelAnswer: An anion is a negatively charged ion.
It is formed when an atom or group of atoms gains one or more electrons.

items.followUp: Write two properties of cathode rays.

rubric.why: Canal rays are streams of positively charged particles.
rubric.description: States that canal rays carry a positive charge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying their positive charge.

rubric.why: Their deflection in a field distinguishes them from uncharged rays and shows their positive charge.
rubric.description: States that canal rays are deflected towards the negative plate in an electric field (or are deflected by electric or magnetic fields).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct property of their deflection.

modelAnswer: Canal rays consist of positively charged particles.
They are deflected towards the negative plate in an electric field.

items.followUp: Write the sub-shell electronic configuration of chlorine (atomic number 17).

rubric.why: The configuration must account for all 11 electrons of sodium in the correct sub-shells.
rubric.description: Gives the complete sub-shell electronic configuration of sodium.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s¹; award 1 mark for a substantially correct configuration with one minor error.

items.followUp: Define a group and a period in the modern periodic table.

rubric.why: A period runs horizontally across the periodic table.
rubric.description: Defines a period as a horizontal row or series.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the horizontal arrangement.

rubric.why: A group runs vertically in the periodic table.
rubric.description: Defines a group as a vertical column or series.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the vertical arrangement.

modelAnswer: A period is a horizontal row of elements in the periodic table.
A group is a vertical column of elements in the periodic table.

items.followUp: Which periods are called very long periods, and how many elements does each contain?

rubric.why: The 4th and 5th periods are the long periods.
rubric.description: Identifies the 4th and 5th periods as long periods.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both periods.

rubric.why: Each of these long periods contains 18 elements.
rubric.description: Gives the number of elements in each long period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating 18 elements in each.

modelAnswer: The 4th and 5th periods are the long periods.

items.followUp: Why does atomic radius generally increase down a group?

rubric.why: Moving down a group adds electron shells, placing the outer electrons farther from the nucleus.
rubric.description: States that additional electron shells increase the distance of the outer electrons from the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the increased-shell or increased-distance reason.

rubric.why: Greater shielding reduces the attraction experienced by the outer electrons, lowering the ionization energy.
rubric.description: Explains that increased shielding or reduced nuclear attraction makes electron removal easier.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the shielding or reduced-attraction reason linked to the decrease in ionization energy.

modelAnswer: Down a group, the number of electron shells increases, so the outer electrons are farther from the nucleus.
Shielding also increases, reducing the nuclear attraction on the outer electrons; therefore, less energy is needed to remove an electron.

items.followUp: What is a double covalent bond? Explain with an example.

rubric.why: A single covalent bond consists of one shared pair of electrons.
rubric.description: Defines a single covalent bond as one pair of electrons shared between two atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that one electron pair is shared.

rubric.why: A correct example should show two atoms forming a bond by sharing one pair of electrons.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example and explains the sharing, such as H₂ or Cl₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example with the shared pair identified.

modelAnswer: A single covalent bond is formed when two atoms share one pair of electrons.
For example, in H₂, each hydrogen atom contributes one electron and the two atoms share the pair, forming an H–H single covalent bond.
